documents.unit: ACU Library (Faculty Guide: AI and ChatGPT)
documents.title: Faculty Guide: AI and ChatGPT: Academic Integrity
documents.summary: A library faculty guide that tells instructors to define acceptable AI use in their own syllabus, lists what a syllabus statement should contain, and gives MLA and APA citation formats for AI. It offers three example statements (AI required, AI prohibited, AI only with permission) borrowed from Harvard and Colorado State. It sets no university-wide rule.
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'Best practice is to define what is acceptable and not acceptable in your class' and supplies three template statements (required, prohibited, use-with-permission) for instructors to choose from, so it decides nothing itself and hands the decision to instructors, with tiers listed.

units.why: The guide gives MLA's format for citing generative AI output ('Name of AI tool, version of AI tool, Company, Date of chat, URL'); this is a citation rule naming tool, version and date, so it is P25 rather than the generic P24 disclosure type. Addressed to students, who do the citing, as guidance (should).
units.anchor: Name of AI tool, version of AI tool, Company, Date of chat, URL.
units.frag_start: Description of chat
units.policy: Students cite AI chats in MLA with the description of the chat as the prompt, then the name and version of the AI tool, the company, the date of the chat and the URL.

units.why: 'MLA also recommends acknowledging when you used the tool in a note or your text' recommends in-text or note acknowledgement of AI use, so it is a disclosure rule (P24) with 'should' modality because it is a recommendation.
units.anchor: MLA also recommends acknowledging when you used the tool in a note or your text

units.why: The guide says to verify 'any sources or citations the tool supplies', which tells students AI output can be wrong and must be checked: P31 fits better than P29 because the focus is verification, not ownership.

units.policy: Students verify any sources or citations the AI tool supplies.

units.why: For saved or shareable chats the guide says 'It may be worthwhile to include the chat's transcript as an appendix', an optional recommendation to keep and submit a transcript, matching P26 with a 'may' modality.
units.anchor: It may be worthwhile to include the chat's transcript as an appendix to your project.

units.why: For chats that cannot be retrieved the guide says to 'follow APA guidelines for citing personal communication' with only an in-text citation; this is a specific citation format rule, so P25 (citation details) rather than P24, and it is guidance (should).
units.anchor: only include an in-text citation and do not include an entry in the references list
units.frag_start: If you have not saved the chat
units.policy: When a chat transcript is not saved or cannot be shared or retrieved, students cite it as personal communication with an in-text citation only and no entry in the references list.

units.why: 'Best practice is to define what is acceptable and not acceptable in your class' tells instructors to state their AI expectations; it is the syllabus-statement type P09 (communicate expectations) with 'should' because it is called a best practice.

units.why: The syllabus statement 'should include' circumstances when AI use is 'permitted or forbidden'; this tells instructors to state the AI rule in the syllabus (P09), and leaves the actual rule to them.
units.anchor: Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden

units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should say under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden.

units.why: The bullet 'How students should cite or credit AI' asks instructors to put citation expectations in the syllabus; I code it P24 (disclosure) since its content is crediting AI, though the actor is the instructor who writes the statement.

units.frag_start: Your policy should include these considerations

units.why: The bullet asks for 'A warning about the technology's tendency toward hallucination', which is the verify-output idea (P31); the accountability half of the bullet is coded as its own unit.

units.why: 'clear rules regarding students' accountability for AI output' is a separate instruction that syllabi set accountability rules, matching P29 (students own what they submit).

units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should include clear rules regarding students' accountability for AI output.

units.why: 'A notice about using AI ethically and responsibly' asks for an ethics notice in the syllabus; closest type is P53 (ethical concerns), though the guide names no specific harm, so P53 is a loose fit chosen over P56 which is institution-level.

units.why: 'the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content' says AI should support students' learning rather than replace it, which matches P32 (AI must not replace thinking) rather than P41 since it is framed as a syllabus content item.
units.anchor: use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content
units.frag_start: Discussion of the need to use
units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should discuss the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content.

units.why: Example 1 states 'I expect you to use AI' and 'some assignments will require it', so AI use is expected and built into work: P02 default stance, 'must' for students, unit stance require.

units.frag_start: I expect you to use AI
units.policy: Students are expected to use AI in this class, and some assignments require it.

units.why: 'Learning to use AI is an emerging skill and I provide tutorials' frames AI use as a skill the course teaches, which is P44 (effective AI use as a skill); it informs rather than binds.

units.why: 'Don't trust anything it says ... assume it is wrong unless you either know the answer or can check' is an instruction to verify AI output, P31, with 'must' force because of the imperative.

units.frag_start: Don’t trust anything it says.

units.why: Students must add 'a paragraph at the end of any assignment that uses AI explaining what you used the AI for and what prompts you used'; this is a disclosure statement that includes prompts, so P25 (tool/prompt details) is chosen over P24 and over P26 since it is a short paragraph, not a log.

units.policy: Students include a paragraph at the end of any assignment that uses AI explaining what they used the AI for and what prompts they used to get the results.

notes: Single library guide, not an official provost policy. Examples 1-3 are quoted third-party sample statements (Harvard Mollick; Colorado State); units from them are coded as the guide's offered templates, not as ACU rules.
